lines.trans: I really feel awkward impersonating a writer.
Stop being afraid, nobody knows his face.
What if Sasha read his smart books?
Then she will admire you even more.
What should I do if she asks about the plot?
Speak mysteriously and look straight into her eyes.
I cannot speak that mysteriously at all.
Just put on these dark glasses, friend.
Do you think dark glasses will solve all problems?
Real writers always wear dark glasses!
Okay, I will try to play this role.
Go ahead and win her heart!
I hope this deception ends well.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be afraid'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: in questions: а вдруг...? = and what if...?
Secondary conversational sense ('what if (in hypotheses)') (а вдруг... = what if...) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся? Мы шли впереди на десять процентов!
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level? We were ten percent ahead!

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

meanings.en: to admire, look up to with wonder
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'схищаться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to admire'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Тогда она будет восхищаться тобой ещё сильнее.
examples.trans: Then she will admire you even more.

meanings.note: direction: идти вперёд = to go forward
colloquial, like a preposition + genitive: лезть вперёд кого-то = to push in ahead of someone
Secondary conversational sense ('forward!, let's go!') (as a command) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Вы взяточник! Вы лезете вперёд больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: You're a bribe-taker! You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.

examples.text: Ну же, смелее вперёд, шеф ждёт твоего ответа!
examples.trans: Come on, boldly forward, the chef is waiting for your answer!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

выдавать.gloss: to hand out, pass off, betray

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'давать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to hand out'.

examples.text: Он выдавал себя за другого человека.
examples.trans: He passed himself off as another person.

examples.text: Мне правда неловко выдавать себя за писателя.
examples.trans: I really feel awkward impersonating a writer.

meanings.note: 'закрывать глаза на' + accusative = to turn a blind eye to

examples.text: Я не буду закрывать на это глаза.
examples.trans: I'm not going to close my eyes to this.

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Secondary conversational sense ('still, yet') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('even (with comparatives)') (ещё больше = even more) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'mysteriously'.

examples.text: Говори загадочно и смотри прямо в глаза.
examples.trans: Speak mysteriously and look straight into her eyes.

examples.text: Я совсем не умею говорить так загадочно.
examples.trans: I cannot speak that mysteriously at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'кончиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to end', forming an aspectual pair with 'заканчиваться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.
деньги закончились = the money ran out

examples.text: Всё, выборы закончились. Тебя начальник ждёт.
examples.trans: That's it, the election is over. Your boss is waiting for you.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('expression') (to run for a second term) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'book' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Put a book under his foot!
I am reading an interesting book.
Samsonov, here, please, is your book.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('all right') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'face', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('person, individual') (formal) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: He has a very kind face.

examples.text: Карамельно-сливочный цвет. Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.

meanings.en: to put on (an item of clothing)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to put on', forming an aspectual pair with 'надевать'.

examples.trans: He put on his best suit.

examples.text: Карамельно-сливочный цвет. Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Secondary conversational sense ('present, current') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
in an awkward or embarrassed manner

examples.text: Да, под такую музыку обниматься немного неловко.
examples.trans: Yes, it is a bit awkward hugging to such music.
It turned out somewhat awkward, Kostya.

meanings.note: needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to carry'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to wear (clothes, glasses)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Плохой бетон привезли. Самсон, ты зря радиаторы носил.
examples.trans: They've delivered bad concrete. Samson, you carried those radiators for nothing.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'deceit, trick' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Declinable plural-only noun meaning 'glasses', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я ничего не вижу! Где мои очки?
examples.trans: I can't see anything! Where are my glasses?

meanings.note: перестань(те)! = stop it!, oh come on!

examples.text: Да перестаньте! Я двадцать лет в карты не играла.
examples.trans: Oh, stop it! I haven't played cards for twenty years.

examples.text: Иначе я перестану давать тебе деньги!
examples.trans: Otherwise I'll stop giving you money!

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'writer', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.trans: A famous writer came to dinner.
A famous writer came for lunch.

examples.text: Для известного русского писателя Виктора Пелевина.
examples.trans: For the famous Russian writer Viktor Pelevin.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'корить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to conquer'.

examples.trans: He wanted to win her heart.

examples.text: Иди вперёд и покори её сердце!
examples.trans: Go ahead and win her heart!

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to try', forming an aspectual pair with 'пробовать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to try, to attempt') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: 'будут проблемы' = there'll be trouble

examples.trans: I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'straight'.
Secondary conversational sense ('straight ahead') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become
Secondary conversational sense ('to solve') (решить задачу) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'role', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Он сыграл главную роль в спектакле.
examples.trans: He played the lead role in the play.

examples.text: Ладно, я попробую сыграть эту роль.
examples.trans: Okay, I will try to play this role.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: у меня сердце = I have a bad heart (colloquial)

examples.text: Мне горько, мне плохо. У меня сердце.
examples.trans: I feel bitter, I feel awful. I have a bad heart.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'strongly'.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to look', forming an aspectual pair with 'посмотреть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to watch') (TV, a film) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'quite'.
Secondary conversational sense ('not at all') (совсем не) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask', paired with 'спрашивать'.

examples.text: А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Ask him where he put the computer lab.

examples.text: Да? А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Really? Then ask him where he put the computer lab.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ыграть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to play'.

examples.trans: The actor played his role wonderfully.

examples.text: Ладно, я попробую сыграть эту роль.
examples.trans: Okay, I will try to play this role.
We will definitely have a big wedding!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'news story', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Телевидение покажет сюжет про вашу дружную семью.
examples.trans: Television will show a story about your united family.

examples.text: Все новые сюжеты уже на вашей почте.
examples.trans: All the new stories are already in your email.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'dark' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: Он надел тёмные очки в солнечный день.
examples.trans: He put on dark glasses on a sunny day.

examples.text: На нём были большие тёмные очки.
examples.trans: He was wearing large dark glasses.

examples.text: Он просто наденет тёмные чёрные очки.
examples.trans: He will simply put on dark black glasses.

уметь.gloss: to know how to, to be able to

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'меть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know how to', forming an aspectual pair with 'суметь'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'мный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('clever, smart').

examples.text: Ты же у нас такая умная!
Ты же у нас такая умная! Скажи, что сделать, я сделаю.
examples.trans: You're the clever one here! Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to read', paired with 'прочитать'.

examples.trans: You don't read the small print.
I am reading an interesting book.

examples.text: Женщина, вы мелкими буквами не читаете. Наша фирма в этом не виновата.
examples.trans: Ma'am, you don't read the small print. Our firm isn't to blame for that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
